audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave level 1 to Skill, levels 2-3 to Cho'Gath, then handed levels 4-5 and 6 back to Skill. The matchup's own prose says the opposite in three separate places: levels 1-2 are Nautilus's, the lane flips to you at 3, and 'you stay ahead all game'.
audit.why: Nautilus at 1-2 has a 1150-range Dredge Line and a passive root on his next auto against you, and Cho'Gath has no dash. From 3 the Rupture-into-Feral-Scream chain lands and Cho'Gath never gives the lane back — he has no percent-health or true damage to crack HP stacking.
audit.corrected: Nautilus / Nautilus / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath, proposed as one atomic group across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side+rating. Deviates from the packet chart only at level 2, where the prose is unambiguous that his hook-plus-root all-in still beats you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase text put Cho'Gath's spike at 'Heartsteel, force fights the moment it completes' and described level 6 in generic terms.
audit.why: The spikes that matter are level 3 (combo online), level 6 (Feast as a true-damage execute his resistances cannot soak) and the first HP item, after which his hook no longer threatens a kill. On his side the spike is Depth Charge at 6 as gank setup, not as a duel win.
audit.corrected: Rewritten into phases[2].why, phases[4].why and phases[5].why with the real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most punishing interaction in this lane was never stated: Feral Scream is a silence, and a silence does not stop auto-attacks, so Staggering Blow's root lands whether or not you silence him. Also missing: Dredge Line is a projectile that pulls Nautilus to terrain on a wall hit, giving him a wall-hop your Rupture cannot answer.
audit.why: The existing text told the player the silence 'blanks his whole kit', which is only true of his casts. A player who trusts that stands in the root chain.
audit.corrected: Stated in tradeBad, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two places call Titan's Wrath his E. It is his W; Riptide is the E.
audit.why: Packet flagged wants.foe[1] ('Use Titan's Wrath (E)'). The same slot error also sits in spikes[1].text. Riptide is what shoves the wave; Titan's Wrath is the shield.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] rewritten to name Riptide (E) as the shove and Titan's Wrath (W) as the shield window; spikes[1].text now labels Titan's Wrath (W).

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was placeholder text with no numbers.
audit.why: Dredge Line at 14s rank 1 is the clock the whole lane runs on — it is the longest cooldown he has before 6 and the only thing that starts a fight.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in for Dredge Line and Riptide.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Nautilus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are his — Dredge Line into the Staggering Blow auto-root chain-locks you and you have no dash, so stay clear of hook range.

edits.before: W silence starts flipping his combo windows. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Still his: hook plus passive root beats you, and Rupture into Feral Scream is not online until 3.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Rupture into Feral Scream lands and a silenced Nautilus cannot hook, shield or ult — the lane turns here at 3.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Trade in Dredge Line's 14s downtime — the moment he sinks the anchor into a minion you get a free Rupture into Feral Scream.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast is point-blank true damage that ignores his armour and MR, so his tank stats do nothing — but Depth Charge (120s) is still free gank setup for his jungler.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Your first HP item plus Carnivore beats his damage — he can CC you, he cannot kill you.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He has no percent-health and no true damage to crack HP stacking, so every Feast stack widens the gap in the straight 1v1.

edits.before: Q under Nautilus's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Rupture him the moment Dredge Line whiffs, Feral Scream so he cannot answer, then E-spike out — Carnivore regens the chip.

edits.before: Whiffing Q and fighting anyway — without the knockup your kit is a slow zone with no teeth.
edits.after: Standing in hook range — the anchor lands, Staggering Blow roots, and silence never stops an auto.

edits.before: His only engage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 14s at rank 1. Bait it into a minion, then take your free trade.

edits.before: Q under Nautilus's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Silence stops casts, not autos — Staggering Blow still roots you, so break contact after Feral Scream instead of standing in it.

edits.before: Nautilus wastes Dredge Line (Hook) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: It is a projectile; strike terrain with it and he pulls himself instead.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: A silence never stops an auto-attack; his passive root lands anyway.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Dredge Line: 14s at rank 1, his only engage — on a terrain hit he pulls himself over the wall instead. - Riptide: 7s at rank 1, his wave shove. - Feral Scream silences casts, never his autos or Staggering Blow.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Respect Nautilus's Dredge Line completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Do not walk into 1150-range hook range for an early Rupture. Last-hit with Vorpal Spikes, let Carnivore top you off, and take your window the moment the anchor sinks into a minion.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. Dodge it. When it is down — Q-W + R him.
edits.after: Feral Scream blanks Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath and Depth Charge — but never his auto-attack root.

edits.before: Your full combo lands — Rupture knockup chains into Feral Scream, and a silenced Nautilus can't fire Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath E, or Depth Charge, so you shut off his whole kit mid-trade.
edits.after: Your full combo lands — Rupture knockup chains into Feral Scream, and a silenced Nautilus can't fire Dredge Line (14s), Titan's Wrath (W), or Depth Charge — but his autos still root.

edits.before: Use Titan's Wrath (E) to shove the wave and trade in his shield window, then look to roam since he can't out-duel you straight
edits.after: Use Riptide (E) to shove the wave and trade inside his Titan's Wrath (W) shield, then roam since he can't out-duel you straight

notes: Whether Dredge Line is stopped by minions is not in Riot's text — the description only says it pulls on colliding with an enemy and pulls Nautilus on colliding with terrain — and needsResearch.minionBlock is null, so I did not claim minion-blocking anywhere; I wrote only 'sink the anchor into a minion' where the existing text already assumed it. Also not asserted: whether Staggering Blow's root or Depth Charge is reduced by tenacity, and whether Feast can be used on an airborne target from Depth Charge. Cho'Gath's kit file flags Rupture as 'grounding'; Riot's description says it pops enemies into the air, so I treated it as a knockup only.
